These tools together allow us to reach Sobolev regularities $s<1/2$, showing for the first time a global existence result in the mass supercritical regime for a class of unbounded, discontinuous data.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Lee, Xueying Yu

item.title: Boundary Blow-up Solutions of Second Order Quasilinear Equation on Infinite Cylinders
item.description: arXiv:2412.18968v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article studies large solutions, for a class of quasi-linear equations involving p-Laplacian on the infinite cylindrical domains. We study the wellposedness of weak large solutions on infinite cylinders by the convergence of large solutions on finite cylinders and observe that any such solution coincides with the large solution on its cross-section. Finally, the results are generalized to a class of operators involving non-linearity in the gradient.
item.dc:creator: Indranil Chowdhury, N. N. Dattatreya

item.title: On the stationary Navier-Stokes equations in distorted pipes under energy-stable outflow boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2506.07331v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The steady motion of a viscous incompressible fluid in distorted pipes, of finite length, is modeled through the Navier-Stokes equations with mixed boundary conditions: the inflow is given by an arbitrary member of the Lions-Magenes class with positive influx, and the fluid motion is subject to a directional do-nothing boundary condition on the outlet, together with the standard no-slip assumption on the remaining walls of the domain. Existence of a weak solution to such Navier-Stokes system is proved without any restriction on the data (that is, inlet velocity and external force) by means of the Leray-Schauder Principle, in which the required a priori estimate is obtained by a contradiction argument that employs Bernoulli's law for solutions of the stationary Euler equations, as well as some properties of harmonic divergence-free vector fields. Under a suitable smallness assumption on the data, we also prove the unique solvability of the boundary-value problem.
item.dc:creator: Alessio Falocchi, Ana Leonor Silvestre, Gianmarco Sperone

item.title: On a fuzzy Landau Equation: II. Solvability results
item.description: arXiv:2507.10288v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article is the second in a series of works on the fuzzy Landau equation, which describes particles interacting through delocalised Coulomb-type collisions. The spatial interaction is modulated by a kernel. We establish the existence of global-in-time H-solutions for exponentially decaying spatial kernels on the whole space and for kernels bounded above and below by positive constants, including periodised kernels on the torus. For the latter class, we further study the propagation of velocity moments and $L^p$-bounds.
item.dc:creator: Manh Hong Duong, Zihui He

item.title: On the extremal functions of second order uncertainty principles: symmetry and symmetry breaking
item.description: arXiv:2508.15221v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper focus on the symmetry and symmetry breaking about the second order Hydrogen Uncertainty Principle. \emph{Firstly}, by choosing a suitable test function, we give a negative answer to the conjecture presented by Cazacu, Flynn and Lam in [\emph{J. Funct. Anal.} \textbf{283} (2022), Paper No. 109659, 37 pp] for $N\in\{2,3\}$, and emphasizing the symmetry breaking phenomenon. \emph{Secondly}, we obtain a family of sharp weighted second order Hydrogen Uncertainty Principle, and prove the extremal functions are radial, which extends the work of Duong and Nguyen [The sharp second order Caffareli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality and stability estimates for the sharp second order uncertainty principle, arXiv:2102.01425].
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Ping Chen, Chun-Lei Tang

item.title: On very weak solutions of certain elliptic systems with double phase growth
item.description: arXiv:2602.03044v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove a higher integrability result for very weak solutions of higher-order elliptic systems involving a double phase operator as the principal part. As a model case, we consider \begin{equation} \int_{\Omega} \left( |D^m u|^{p-2}D^m u + a(x)|D^m u|^{q-2}D^m u \right) \cdot D^m \varphi = 0 \quad \text{for any } \varphi \in C_c^{\infty}(\Omega), \end{equation} where $n,\,m \in \mathbb{N},\ n\ge 2,\,1 < p \le q < \infty,\,\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is an open set and $a:\Omega \rightarrow [0,\infty)$ is a measurable function. We extend the result of Baasandorj, Byun and Kim (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2023) with respect to the derivative order, the coefficient class and the growth conditions. The proof is based on a construction of an appropriate test function by the Lipschitz truncation technique, a deduction of a reverse H\"older inequality and an application of Gehring's lemma. To this end, we establish estimates for weighted mean value polynomials and sharp Sobolev--Poincar\'e-type inequalities for the double phase operator.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiki Kaiho

item.title: Boundary Blowup Solutions for the Finsler p-Laplacian: Wellposedness and Asymptotic Behaviour
item.description: arXiv:2605.22345v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the existence of large (boundary blow-up) solutions to semilinear equations involving the Finsler p-Laplacian on bounded domains with sufficiently smooth boundaries. We establish a Keller-Osserman-type condition that ensures the existence of such solutions, and show that this condition retains the same integrability as that of the p-Laplacian. We examine the influence of the anisotropic norm underlying the Finsler p-Laplacian on the boundary behaviour of the solution, then derive asymptotic estimates for large solutions near the boundary of the domain. Using these boundary asymptotics, we prove uniqueness results for power-type nonlinearities.
item.dc:creator: N N Dattatreya

item.title: Spreading speeds for prey-predator systems in a shifting environment: a short proof
item.description: arXiv:2606.14059v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This note is concerned with the spreading speed of the predator component in a class of prey-predator reaction-diffusion systems with spatiotemporal heterogeneity depending on a moving variable. The main difficulty is that the full system lacks a direct comparison principle. We establish a pointwise estimate showing that the prey density is close to its carrying capacity wherever the predator density is sufficiently small. This allows us to compare solutions of the system with those of scalar Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments. Consequently, we obtain an explicit formula for the spreading speed of the predator. In particular, for nonmonotone shifting environments, locking and nonlocal pulling phenomena may occur.
item.dc:creator: Zhucheng Jin

item.title: Spreading speeds for nonlocal Fisher-KPP equations with time-dependent asymmetric kernels
item.description: arXiv:2606.15226v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish spreading speeds for a nonlocal Fisher-KPP equation with measurable time-dependent asymmetric kernels, without imposing an inequality between growth and diffusion or requiring the kernel to be positive near the origin. The kernel has a time independent upper bound which is thin-tailed. Both the kernel and the linear growth rate have uniform means. Under these assumptions, we determine the exact rightward and leftward spreading speeds and prove convergence to the positive equilibrium inside the spreading interval. The proof is based on comparison arguments and a family of compactly supported subsolutions. Explicit examples show that time-dependent dispersal kernels with the same time average can exhibit different propagation behaviors.
item.dc:creator: Zhucheng Jin, Tao Zhou

item.title: The Wave Kinetic Theory for Quasilinear MMT Equation
item.description:

We consider Gaussian random initial data and work in the joint limit $L	o\infty$ with $\alpha=\lambda^2L^{-1}	o0$. The quasilinear structure leads to unavoidable derivative loss, which prevents the direct construction of solutions via iteration of the Duhamel formula. item.dc:creator: Huaxiang L\"u

item.title: Long-Time Dispersion and Threshold Resonances for the Landau Hamiltonian on the Hyperbolic Plane
item.description: arXiv:2609.12999v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A uniform magnetic field completely suppresses long-time dispersion for the Euclidean Landau Hamiltonian. We show that negative curvature fundamentally changes this behavior. For the Landau Hamiltonian with arbitrary field strength $B\in\mathbb R$ on the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb H$, we establish sharp dispersive estimates for the Schr\"odinger evolution on the absolutely continuous spectral subspace. The decay is $|t|^{-1}$ at short times and, strikingly, improves to $|t|^{-3/2}$ at large times whenever $B\notin\frac12+\mathbb Z$. At half-integer fields, we identify a threshold resonance and isolate its leading contribution, which yields the slower but sharp rate $|t|^{-1/2}$. Thus the long-time dynamics exhibit a resonance-driven dichotomy with no analogue in the flat constant-field problem. Our analysis is based on an explicit representation of the magnetic Schr\"odinger kernel together with a precise separation of the Landau levels and threshold profile. As a further consequence, for every nonthreshold field we obtain global-in-time Strichartz estimates on the absolutely continuous spectral subspace throughout the full hyperbolic admissible region.
item.dc:creator: Huanqing Guo, Haoran Wang, Junyong Zhang, Jiqiang Zheng

item.title: An explicit solution of the five-expert prediction PDE and the exact optimality set of COMB
item.description: arXiv:2609.14892v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we derive an explicit solution of the stationary prediction with expert advice PDE for five experts. The formula is given in three regions. In the first two regions, it is the four-expert solution plus a single integral with an elementary positive density. In the third region, it is a finite sum of hyperbolic products whose coefficients are determined by one scalar quadrature. Our formula establishes that the rank ordered adversary $(1,0,1,0,0)$ achieves the Hamiltonian maximum in the PDE everywhere in the ordered sector, while the COMB strategy $(1,0,1,0,1)$ is optimal only on a lower dimensional subset of the sector (where $x_1=x_2$ and $x_3=x_4$). The verification of the Hamiltonian inequalities is a tedious task, part of which is completed with a computer assisted proof. The verification reduces to 21 scalar inequalities, which we prove using 147 exact rational Bernstein polynomial certificates. The exact certificates and their independent arithmetic checks are included in a supplement to this paper, and a Lean 4 formalization machine-checks the verification and both main theorems, apart from the viscosity characterization.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Calder, Nadejda Drenska

item.title: Critical semilinear damped wave equations beyond moduli of continuity
item.description: arXiv:2609.27862v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for semilinear classical damped wave equations with general nonnegative nondecreasing nonlinearities, without imposing a modulus-of-continuity structure or convexity. A Dini-type integral condition expressed directly in terms of the nonlinearity gives small data global in-time existence and extends the nonlinear framework of Ebert--Girardi--Reissig [Math. Ann. 378 (2020), 1311--1326]. When this Dini-type integral diverges and the effective total mass of the initial data is positive, convergence of the Keller--Osserman tail integral is necessary and sufficient for finite-time blow-up of the maximal mild Sobolev solution, particularly, divergence of the tail integral gives global grow-up. The resulting integral criteria distinguish the contributions of the nonlinearity near zero and at infinity in governing small data global in-time existence with diffusion decay, global grow-up, and finite-time blow-up.
item.dc:creator: Wenhui Chen

item.title: Global Well-Posedness and Uniform Long-Time Control for a Class of Periodic NLS-Dysthe Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.14786v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a class of periodic NLS-Dysthe equations of the form $i\partial_tu+a\partial_x^2u+b|u|^2u+i\varepsilon(c\partial_x^3u+d|u|^2\partial_xu+eu^2\partial_x\overline{u})=0$ with $x\in\mathbb T$, $a,b,c,d,e\in\mathbb R$, $abc\neq0$, and $\varepsilon>0$. For $0<\varepsilon\ll1$, equations of this type arise as higher-order modulation models for some nonlinear dispersive PDEs, including the Klein-Gordon equation and the Serre-Green-Naghdi equation modeling the evolution of nonlinear shallow water waves. We prove local well-posedness in $H^s(\mathbb T)$ for $s>3/2$ for arbitrary admissible coefficients, and establish an $H^1$ continuation criterion for $s\ge2$. Under the additional assumption $e\neq0$, a lower-order conservation law provides uniform $H^1$ control and, together with the continuation criterion, yields global well-posedness for $s\ge2$. Unlike the previous $H^1$ global theory based on Takaoka's periodic well-posedness estimates (2000), our result does not require any non-resonance condition on the coefficients. Our approach relies on the construction of modified higher-order energies, following the strategy developed for the generalized KdV equation by Planchon, Tzvetkov and Visciglia (2023) and for the generalized DNLS equation by Hayashi, Ozawa and Visciglia (2025). Motivated by higher-order modulation theory, we exploit the conservation laws of cubic NLS and their invariance under the commuting complex mKdV flow to establish Sobolev bounds uniform in the modulation parameter $\varepsilon$ on time intervals of order $\varepsilon^{-1}$. This corresponds to physical times of order $\varepsilon^{-3}$, which is the natural time scale anticipated for the NLS-Dysthe approximation.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Belloni, Filippo Giuliani

item.title: Propagation of Sobolev Regularity for Integral-Invariant Weak Solutions of the Linear Transport Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.39527v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Previous work strengthened the time integrability of integral-invariant weak solutions from L^1 to L^\infty within a spatial L^2 framework.This paper studies the propagation of Sobolev regularity for integral-invariant weak solutions of the conservative linear scalar transport equation.We first derive a representation formula along the flow and a distributional equation from integral identities against adjoint-transported test functions on domains moving with the same characteristic flow,and relate the weak formulation in time, including an endpoint term for the initial data, to representatives satisfying the pointwise-in-time integral definition.We then give a unified proof for k=1,2:under u_0\in H^k(\Omega_0)and Assumption \mathsf A_{k+1},the pullback of the solution belongs to C^1([0,T];H^k(\Omega_0)),the material derivative has spatial $H^k$ regularity,and the Eulerian time derivative has spatial H^{k-1} regularity.The corresponding time continuity is understood after pullback to the fixed domain by the flow.In both cases, U\in H^1(Q);when k=2, we further obtain \nabla_xU\in H^1(Q;\R^d).The pullback differentiability and the spatial estimates for the material derivativeprovide information beyond first-order space-time Sobolev regularity alone.The proof combines estimates for the characteristic flow with Sobolev product and composition rules.Under the additional assumption that the zero extension of the initial data belongs to H^2(\R^d),we also establish $H^1(0,T;H^1(\R^d))$ regularity in the fixed ambient space.Counterexamples show that these results concern regularity propagation under additional assumptions: general L^2 initial data do not automatically yield spatial smoothing,and spatial regularity of the material derivative cannot replace the corresponding regularity of the Eulerian time derivative.
item.dc:creator: Zhengrong Xie

item.title: Quantitative Propagation of Chaos for Singular Interacting Particle Systems Driven by Fractional Brownian Motion
item.description: arXiv:2403.05454v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider interacting systems particle driven by i.i.d. fractional Brownian motions, subject to irregular, possibly distributional, pairwise interactions. We show propagation of chaos and mean field convergence to the law of the associated McKean--Vlasov equation, as the number of particles $N\to\infty$, with quantitative sharp rates of order $N^{-1/2}$. Our results hold for a wide class of possibly time-dependent interactions, which are only assumed to satisfy a Besov-type regularity, related to the Hurst parameter $H\in (0,+\infty)\setminus \mathbb{N}$ of the driving noises. In particular, as $H$ decreases to $0$, interaction kernels of arbitrary singularity can be considered, a phenomenon frequently observed in regularization by noise results. Our proofs rely on a combinations of Sznitman's direct comparison argument with stochastic sewing techniques.
item.dc:creator: Lucio Galeati, Khoa L\^e, Avi Mayorcas

item.title: A $Tb$ type theorem for suppressed kernels
item.description: arXiv:2606.26401v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, a non-homogeneous $Tb$ type theorem for arbitrary dimensional Calder\'on-Zygmund singular integral operators is proved. This is an extension of an analogous non-homogeneous $Tb$ theorem for the Cauchy transform, in the planar setting, due to Nazarov, Treil and Volberg. The novelties of the present work are the change of dimension and the fact that the operators to which the theorem applies are not necessarily antisymmetric. The techniques used in the proof include, among others, suppressed kernels, decompositions in $L^2(\mu)$, where $\mu$ is a Radon measure in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and a probabilistic argument resulting from taking averages of the operators involved.
item.dc:creator: Marina Fern\`andez-Vilaseca

item.title: Monge's transport problem in synthetic Lorentzian spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2609.17592v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the existence of solutions to the Lorentzian Monge problem on synthetic Lorentzian spacetimes that satisfy the forward timelike measure contraction property $TMCP^+(K,N)$. The cost for this problem is the time separation function $\ell(x,y)$ (the Lorentz distance), which represents the maximum amount a particle can age when traveling from $x$ to $y$. The solution is based on the needle decomposition technique, and amounts to a reduction of the full problem to its one-dimensional counterparts. As an application of needle decomposition, we introduce the blended $TMCP$ condition, and obtain a quantitative refinement of the synthetic Hawking singularity theorem. We additionally prove a timelike nonbranching reversibility theorem for $TCD_p(K,N)$ spacetimes, showing that forward $p$-essentially nonbranching spacetimes are backward $p$-essentially nonbranching.

item.title: Sparse domination modulo polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.09771v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a sparse domination theory that captures both local polynomial approximation and cancellation of the input below the scale of each sparse cube. Its coefficients are percentiles of localized smooth maximal functions of the input minus its local polynomial approximation, combining features of mean-oscillation sparse bounds and of the cancellative sparse bounds of Conde-Alonso, Lorist and Rey. Using wavelet representations, we characterize the Calder\'on-Zygmund operators whose derivatives admit these bounds by explicit polynomial testing conditions. In the homogeneous setting, the same conditions characterize weighted Hardy-Sobolev inequalities with linear dependence on the $A_\infty$ characteristic. This quantitative dependence detects the transition from BMO to $L^\infty$ testing conditions that Lerner found for pointwise bounds by Riesz potentials, a distinction that qualitative weighted estimates cannot recover. In the inhomogeneous setting, we prove corresponding weighted inequalities and show that they are strictly weaker than pointwise sparse domination from the second derivative order onward. Consequences include Hardy-Sobolev estimates below the Banach range, sharp weighted Sobolev inequalities, and pointwise bounds by Riesz potentials.
